content.introduction: The S&P 500 declined 0.8% for the week, marking four consecutive sessions of falling averages. The decline was attributed to macroeconomic factors influencing US borrowing costs, according to Lyngen. However, the market ended the week on a high note, with the S&P 500 rising 0.9% on Friday, driven by positive consumer price index data and lower oil futures. The sources do not provide a definitive reason for the S&P 500's decline on the specific date of November 9, 2026.
body:
The three major averages had fallen for four consecutive sessions. For the Dow, it was the longest daily losing streak since late April. Week to date, the Dow fell 1.6% and the S&P 500 declined 0.8%. The Nasdaq fell about 0.7%, marking its first negative week in three sessions. [...] Similarly, shares for Dell Technologies are almost up by 11% after RBC initiated coverage of the stock and gave an outperform rating. Seagate Technology is down over 3.4% and the worst performing stock in the S&P 500 and Nasdaq.

Cisco Systems is the biggest percentage gainer in the Dow today, up 4.1% with Caterpillar contributing the most to the Dow's upside by 95 points. Meanwhile UnitedHealth, Amgen and Johnson & Johnson are down in the Dow.

— Ananya Chetia [...] "For the moment, the fiscal narrative is a powerful one and is having a historically disproportionate influence on the level of US borrowing costs," Lyngen said, adding that they were reluctant to bet against the bearish momentum until the market gets through the latest supply, inflation data and Fed decision.

— Lee Ying Shan

"We've seen this trend multiple times where macro factors will induce a selloff, but it's typically bought back pretty quickly when investors realize that they're able to buy the market on the dip," says Will Rhind, CEO of GraniteShares.

"We're dealing with a market which is fundamentally strong, at least as far as earnings are concerned, and particularly tech earnings," he adds.

The equity market's fundamental strength will be put to the test yet again with next week's Fed policy meeting. [...] Sept. 11, 2026 at 7:30pm ET

Sept. 11, 4:07pm ET

The stock market ended the week on a high note, with all three major indexes taking part in a broad rally on Friday.

The S&P 500 rose 0.9%. The Nasdaq Composite gained 1%. The Dow Jones Industrial Average gained 1%, or 508 points.

Stocks ticked higher after August's consumer price index data fueled a surge in odds that the Fed will raise rates, removing some uncertainty from the market. [...] Another contributing factor to Friday's equity gains was West Texas Intermediate oil futures ticking lower, while the rise in Brent crude futures slowed. Saudi Arabia's Ministry of Energy announced a temporary suspension of flows through the the East-West Pipeline, though oil futures were roughly unchanged on the news. Oil prices still remained near multi-month highs alongside high Treasury yields.
